Needs changes before merge.

This is a safety-tier review. The change affects wire gouge checks and the post refusal. The code review found no other blocker.

The PR trial-merges cleanly with upstream/main `a35c9cb8197f484fca0f8311610bdc8594111a0f`. All tests below ran locally on that trial merge. No GitHub runner was used.

**Results**

- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: PASS. All 627 steps completed in 37.1 minutes. The 626 test targets passed 4,383 tests; 47 tests were ignored.
- The gate built the app test binaries and ran the sim library: 224 tests passed.
- `cargo clippy -j 16 -p camcraft-sim -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: PASS.
- Heavy gate: dry run only. It selects 236 steps for the app and motion lanes, including the release build. The heavy and light lanes were not run within this review's time budget. This is not a pass.

The wire suites all passed:

| App suite | Passed |
|---|---:|
| wire_4axis | 8 |
| wire_burnout | 3 |
| wire_contour | 8 |
| wire_fans | 2 |
| wire_post | 12 |
| wire_readers | 7 |
| wire_stamp | 7 |
| wire_tabs | 4 |
| wire_taper | 10 |
| wire_taper_angle | 5 |
| wire_taper_chord | 3 |
| wire_tool | 5 |
| wire_verify | 3 |
| wire_verify_tol | 2 |

**Extra suites run**

No fixture directory or importer code changed. Neither extra selection rule requires another suite. I also ran `cargo test -j 16 -p camcraft-app --test wire_taper_chord` for each mutation and each restoration.

**Mutations repeated independently**

- Set the constant-taper tolerance to zero: RED. The true-angle test and the undercut test failed. Restored: GREEN, all 3 tests passed.
- Disable the undercut branch: RED. The undercut test failed because the program posted. Restored: GREEN, all 3 tests passed.

The source was restored after each mutation. `git diff --exit-code` passed after the checks. No golden changed. There were no moved G-code or CL goldens to inspect.

**Requested before merge**

1. `crates/sim/src/verify/wire/mod.rs:306`: Required heavy test results are missing. Upstream main's **Heavy lanes at review** rule requires the reached heavy tests to pass before the PR is ready. Run `cargo xtask gate heavy --base upstream/main` on the final head. Add the lane results to the PR body. The dry run reaches the app and motion lanes; the body reports neither lane. Complete the light lane check at review time as required by **The light lane**.

The body states the remaining limits: no real STEP die, no recorded coarse-chord test, and no real EDM control. No UI file changed, so before/after screenshots are not required.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.

Addressed: The missing heavy and light results are now in the PR body.

- Final head: `74c469d186840e201828a7e7c3888ea3683638ea`.
- Heavy: PASS. All 241 steps completed. Motion passed 59 tests. App passed 43 tests. No step failed.
- The heavy gate also confirmed six registered expected failures for #1950 and #2849. The gate accepted these checks.
- Light: PASS. Both light twins passed. All 3 steps completed. No step failed.
- Quick: PASS. All 639 steps completed. 4,449 tests passed; 47 were ignored.
- Clippy: PASS for sim and app, all targets, with warnings denied.

The merge from upstream/main keeps both added wire helpers unchanged. The new upstream depth-test fixture now sets `taper_chord: false`. Sim library compilation was RED with E0063 before this field was added. All 232 sim library tests passed after the change.

The worktree and goldens are clean. No review evidence was committed. The PR remains a draft. Please review this head again.

Ready for the maintainer to merge.

This is a safety-tier review. The change affects wire gouge checks and the post refusal. I found no blocker.

The PR trial-merges cleanly with upstream/main `6e1805bfdae52fcfea71a946d381dfbfdefc79f5`. I checked the laws from that main revision. All checks below ran locally in `.claude/worktrees/review-3225`. No GitHub runner was used.

**What looks good**

- Constant-taper cuts use the model's chord tolerance. Four-axis cuts keep their stated tolerance.
- The undercut finding blocks the post. The new tests check the true angle, an undercut, and a gouge.
- The decision record states the reason and the alternatives.

**Local results on the trial merge**

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` | PASS: 669 steps, 4,680 tests passed, 47 ignored, zero failures; 69.3 minutes |
| Sim library, in the quick gate | PASS: 232 tests |
| `wire_taper_chord`, in the quick gate | PASS: 3 tests |
| Existing wire suites, in the quick gate | PASS: four-axis, burnout, contour, DXF selection, fans, ISO decimal, post, readers, stamp, tabs, taper, taper angle, tool, verify, verify tolerance |
| `cargo clippy -j 8 -p camcraft-sim -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings` | PASS |
| `cargo xtask gate light` | PASS: both light twins; 3 steps, zero failures; 9.0 minutes |

**Earlier finding**

The missing heavy results are now in the PR body for this final head. The author reports all 241 heavy steps passed. The motion lane passed 59 tests. The app lane passed 43 tests. The gate also confirmed six registered expected failures for #1950 and #2849. Those checks are not passing product tests.

This resolves the earlier missing-evidence finding. I did not repeat the full heavy lanes in this review. I repeated the light lane locally.

**Extra suites run**

No test data, fixture directory, golden directory, or importer code changed. Neither extra selection rule requires another suite. I ran `cargo test -j 8 -p camcraft-app --test wire_taper_chord` for each mutation and each restoration.

**Mutations repeated independently**

1. Set the constant-taper chord allowance to zero: RED. The true-angle and undercut tests failed. Restored: GREEN, all 3 tests passed.
2. Disable the undercut call: RED. The undercut test failed because the program posted. Restored: GREEN, all 3 tests passed.

I restored the sources after each mutation. `git diff --exit-code` passed after restoration and after the final checks. No G-code or CL golden changed. There were no moved goldens to inspect line by line.

**Requested before merge**

None.

**Limits**

The PR states that the real STEP die, a recorded coarser chord, and a real EDM control were not exercised. The new fixture is a synthetic punch. No UI file changed, so before/after screenshots are not required.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.

<!-- pr-reviewer: 74c469d186840e201828a7e7c3888ea3683638ea -->
Post-merge second safety read (Opus, read-only): clean

This read is after the merge (f3f066ebb). It is read-only. I did not build or run tests. I read the PR body, the diff, and the changed files at 74c469d18.

**Verdict.** I found no path that lets a gouge pass or posts wrong output. I found two latent notes. Neither blocks.

**1. The tolerance change cannot hide a real gouge past the importer's promise.**
- `wire_verify::taper_chord` gives `step::CHORD_CAP` (0.005 mm) for a constant-taper cut on a full-fidelity model. A 4-axis cut keeps its stated tolerance. A cut with no taper keeps 0.
- `judge` still refuses a tolerance that is not finite, is negative, or is not below the kerf offset (`Unreadable`). The unknown-fidelity sentinel (`UNKNOWN_MM`) thus gives a refusal, not a pass.
- A gouge past the chord tolerance stays a `WireFinding::Gouge` and blocks the post. The guard test `a_taper_short_of_the_wall_still_gouges` pins this.
- The true-surface bound for a taper cut is now the chord plus the sagitta, at most `DEV_TOL` (0.01 mm). This is the same bound that the program sim forgives. The decision record `docs/decisions/3210-wire-taper-chord.md` states the choice.

**2. The new refusal is visible and names the cause.**
- `WireFinding::Undercut` says the move, the stand-off, the position, the height, the tolerance and the remedy. It goes into `v.findings`, so it blocks the post as each wire finding does.
- `undercut::judge` drops non-finite readings. If all readings of a move are non-finite, the law skips that move. This is not a silent pass: the kerf law runs independently, and the undercut law is new extra coverage.
- `taper_deg` is validated as finite and below 90 deg at the command (`types/wire_edm.rs:202`).

**3. No `unwrap`, `expect` or `panic!` on user paths.** The new non-test code uses `get` and `let ... else`. There is no direct index.

**4. The pinning tests cannot pass without the fix.** The first two tests assert text that did not exist before ("the model's chord tolerance", "wire undercut"). The PR body also gives the red readings before the fix and three mutations.

**5. Goldens and examples.** No `.nc`, `.cl` or snapshot file changed. Each changed test fixture only adds `taper_chord: false`.

**6. The earlier wire changes on main.**
- #3226 (gouge depth reading): this PR keeps its "enters the part by" text and adds the `chord` field. Each `Gouge` construction on main sets the field.
- #3229 (decimal point) and #3263 (non-finite wire numbers): these change the post side. This PR changes the verify side only, so there is no overlap.
- On main, each `WireJob` literal has `taper_chord`. The wire verify files on main are equal to the PR head.

**Latent notes (not blocking, no change requested here):**
- N1. `taper_chord` folds a coarser chord from `model_fidelity::chord_of` with `f64::max`. This makes the taper tolerance looser on a reduced-fidelity model. The #864 law says that a coarse model makes a verdict stricter, never looser. Today this has no effect on output: `fidelity_law::excess_aware` is `false` for `Section::WireEdm`, so `model_fidelity::law::op_problem` refuses each wire operation on a reduced model at the post. When #532 makes the wire kerf law excess-aware, this fold must change to the #864 rule, or a gouge up to the coarse chord can pass. Also, `taper_chord` reads only the source entities. `op_coarse` reads the setup stock too.
- N2. On an unknown-fidelity model, the verdict line says "the verify tolerance 1000000000000 mm is not zero or a positive number below the kerf offset". The gate refusal (`UNKNOWN_NOTE`) is the correct cause and also blocks. The wire line could name the unknown fidelity instead.

Not exercised by this read: a build, a test run, a real STEP import, a die (conical hole) fixture.
